breeding_policy.philosophy: Select by performance, not pedigree. Breed reputation means nothing — survival on THIS property decides.

selection_hierarchy.description: Can it survive parasites with minimal intervention? FAMACHA 1-2 without deworming = gold. FAMACHA 4-5 requiring treatment = cull candidate.
Does it shed its coat? Observed coat, not calculated from breed. Score at weaning: 1=full wool, 5=full shed.
Genetic background for context. Informs but does not decide. A mutt with FAMACHA 1 beats a purebred Katahdin with FAMACHA 5.
Tiebreaker. Given two animals equal in parasites, coat, and breed — choose the meatiest.

hard_lessons: St Croix purchased and brought to property DIED OF PARASITES. Breed reputation ≠ individual resistance.
Barbados Black Belly purchased and brought to property DIED OF PARASITES. Same lesson.
Windlestone Dorper (exceptional South African bloodlines) are EXTREMELY VULNERABLE to parasites despite being hair sheep. Hair coat ≠ parasite resistance. Independent traits.
GG and Rocky are alive because owner skill improved, not because they are resistant. They require aggressive treatment to survive.
Cracker coat type is VARIABLE per individual — Merrie sheds, 00110 does not. Cannot classify per breed.
Every animal currently alive has survived Florida parasite pressure. That survival IS the genetics that work.
Buying outside genetics is HIGH RISK. Even 'resistant' breeds die here. Safest investment is what's already proven on this land.

Spring 2026 is an extreme drought. Animals scoring FAMACHA 4-5 during DRY season (lowest parasite pressure) will be catastrophically worse when rains return. Dry-season FAMACHA failures are the strongest cull signal.

hard_lessons.detail: Drought-season FAMACHA audit identified 5 living animals scoring FAMACHA 5 in the last 60 days plus 4 additional weak-resistance adults to watch. Recommendation document at data/2026_drought_cull_list.md. Pattern: Kelsier-sired Serendipity twins both failed (sire 'gold standard' + susceptible-dam = susceptible lambs) — confirms dam genetics dominate parasite vulnerability in this flock. GG's 3rd emergency in the cohort closes the case for culling her despite owner-skill keeping her alive.

Untreated-at-source-farm survival is a positive but ambiguous signal. Survivorship bias (animals that died untreated were not measured) and lower-pressure microenvironments can both inflate apparent resistance. Owner observation: animals brought to Manatee Creek from Danny's place (no-treatment philosophy) have sometimes struggled here. Rule: discount external 'never-treated' resistance claims by ~30-40% until one full Manatee Creek wet-season cycle establishes on-property data. Apply transplant-watch protocol (weekly FAMACHA + day 30/60 FEC + no early advancement) to all newly-arrived purchased or transferred animals from any external source.
